faq.question: How is HRA exemption calculated?
faq.answer: It's the lowest of three amounts: the HRA you received, 50% of salary (40% outside the eight listed cities), and rent paid minus 10% of salary. Salary means basic pay plus retirement-linked DA and fixed commission. The rest of the HRA is taxable.

faq.question: Which cities get the 50% HRA limit from April 2026?
faq.answer: Delhi, Mumbai, Kolkata and Chennai, plus Bengaluru, Hyderabad, Pune and Ahmedabad, which were added by the Income-tax Rules 2026. Every other city uses 40%.

faq.question: Can I claim HRA in the new tax regime?
faq.answer: No. HRA exemption is available only under the old regime. In the new regime the full allowance is taxable.

faq.question: Do I need my landlord's PAN for HRA?
faq.answer: Yes, if the rent you pay is more than ₹1 lakh in the year. If you rent from a relative, you also need to declare the relationship in Form 124 under the 2026 rules.

faq.question: What if I paid rent for only part of the year?
faq.answer: Calculate the exemption only for the months you rented, using the salary and HRA for those months. Calculating over the full year subtracts 10% of salary for months without rent and can understate the exemption.
